subStrands.name: Cubes and Cube Roots
specificLearningOutcomes: Determine cubes of numbers by multiplication
Determine cube roots of numbers by factor method
Apply cubes and cube roots to real-life situations
keyInquiryQuestions: Where do we use cubes and cube roots in real life?

subStrands.name: Indices and Logarithms
specificLearningOutcomes: Apply laws of indices to simplify expressions
Use logarithm tables/laws to simplify calculations
subStrands.notes: Sub-strand is deep enough that the design itself breaks it into further named topics — use subSubStrands as the skill-granularity unit here, not the parent sub-strand.

_comment_learningExperiences_fields: The three fields below (learningExperiences, linkedLearningAreas, scopeNotes) were added 2026-08-15 per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md. They are optional but STRONGLY expected on every sub-strand entry written from now on — this is where the real enumerated content pools live in a KICD design (almost always inside parentheses in the Suggested Learning Experiences column), and omitting them was the root cause of Grade 7 Integrated Science SI.3 shipping with 5 SI units and 3 basic skills when the source design names 7 and 7 respectively. See the worked example below, transcribed verbatim from designs/GRADE.7.INTEGRATED.SCIENCE.pdf.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Laboratory apparatus and instruments
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the basic skills in science
Use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory
Use the SI units for basic and derived quantities in science
Appreciate consumer protection when handling different apparatus, instruments and other materials in day to day life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are basic skills in science important?
How are quantities in science expressed?
learningExperiences: Discuss the use of basic skills in science (manipulative, observation, measurement, classification, prediction, communication and conclusion skills)

Practice use and care for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory, for heating, measuring mass, temperature, length, volume, weight, magnification and time (include parts, functions and care of a light microscope; and parts of a bunsen burner)

Carry out activities on measurements of basic quantities and express them in the International System of Units (SI): length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, light intensity
Carry out activities to determine derived units from basic units: area, volume, speed, density
Collect packaging featuring labels of quantities and discuss the importance of the information on labels
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — measurement skills linked to measurements of various quantities in Mathematics
Agriculture and Nutrition — manipulative and measurement skills linked to measurements of ingredients when preparing meals
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric's 'Meets expectations' row for apparatus reads 'uses and cares for apparatus and instruments in the laboratory correctly' — confirms care (not just identification) is part of the tested competency.
subStrands.notes: Case study written up in full in CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md — this sub-strand is what the guide exists to fix.
